conclusion: CNC-02 is showing intermittent vibration exceeding the 4.50 mm/s threshold: alarms at tick 914 (4.58 mm/s) and tick 919 (4.51 mm/s), with readings below threshold in between (915–918, 920). Load is stable (~53–57%, E6), so this is not load-driven process variation. No prior alarms before 914 (E3, E7), so this is a new/developing pattern rather than a one-off transient (H1) or long-standing variation (H4). A sensor fault (H3) is not ruled out but unsupported. One more check — spindle temperature during the same window — could confirm a mechanical cause (overheating bearing) and raise confidence to intervene, or support a sensor fault if temperature is normal.

anomaly: 3 of the last 10 jobs failed inspection (jobs 11, 13, 15)
conclusion: A real anomaly began at the batch 1→batch 2 boundary (around tick 1086): every job 1–9 passed inspection (E12), job 10 passed (E10), then jobs 11, 13 and 15 failed while jobs 12 and 14 passed (E10). Every job runs through all six CNC machines in sequence (CNC-01 … CNC-06) — jobs 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 all visit every machine (E3, E4, E7, E8) — so no single machine is implicated and a per-machine part replacement is not indicated. The failures alternate by job within batch 2, which fits a batch-boundary configuration/input/per-job condition (H1) rather than a worn component (H2 contradicted by E4/E7/E8) or normal variation (H3 contradicted by E10/E12). Inspections record only pass/fail, so no failure reason is available for jobs 11, 13, 15 (Q6/Q11 unresolved), and the failures are spaced one job apart rather than clustered at shift start/end, so a time-of-day/warm-up effect (Q5/H4) is not supported. Confidence 0.90.

anomaly: 3 of the last 10 jobs failed inspection (jobs 11, 12, 13)
conclusion: Jobs 11, 12, and 13 all failed inspection while jobs 1-10 all passed (E2, H3 at 0.95). All three failing jobs passed through CNC-06 immediately before inspection (E3, E7), and CNC-06 was fine for job 10 (finished 999, passed at 1000) but jobs 11-13 failed after using it. CNC-05's following_error is stable across the batch boundary (E4 vs E9), which argues against CNC-05 (H2, only 0.20) and against a sudden CNC-05 mechanical fault. Confidence in any specific causal fix is below 0.90, so I cannot intervene yet. One targeted sensor check on CNC-06 could confirm or rule it out and change the recommendation.

anomaly: 3 of the last 4 jobs failed inspection (jobs 1, 2, 4)
conclusion: Jobs 1, 2, and 4 genuinely failed inspection while job 3 passed. All four jobs ran through the identical CNC-01 → CNC-02 → CNC-03 → CNC-04 → CNC-05 sequence before inspection (E5, E6, E7, E9), and job 3 passed through CNC-05 (ticks 396–470) immediately after job 2 failed there (tick 396) and before job 4 failed (tick 547), so a persistent CNC-05 fault is ruled out. CNC-05 vibration and following_error are elevated but steady across ticks 240–550 with no spike at the failure ticks (E10, E11, E12). The pattern is most consistent with a job-specific production difference (material lot, parameters, operator, or shift) — H1 — rather than an inspection malfunction (job 3 passed between two failures) or one broken machine. Confidence is about 0.70, below the 0.90 threshold for intervene, and none of the available actions (replace_bearing, reset_setting, replace_servo_drive, repair_hydraulics) addresses a material/lot/parameter cause. Evidence that would raise confidence: job parameter/lot records comparing job 3 to jobs 1, 2, 4, and sensor trends for CNC-01 through CNC-04 during the relevant job windows.

conclusion: Intermittent inspection failures on batch 2: jobs 14 (tick 1354), 19 (1702), and 20 (1768) failed inspection while jobs 15-18 passed between them (E2, E3), so the fault is condition-dependent/intermittent rather than progressive degradation (H4 is weakened by the passes between failures). All three failing jobs finished on CNC-07 immediately before inspection - job 14 finished CNC-07 at 1353 then failed at 1354; job 19 finished CNC-07 at 1701 then failed at 1702; job 20 finished CNC-07 at 1767 then failed at 1768 (E6, E8) - but it is unverified whether passing jobs 17 and 18 also used CNC-07 (Q13 open) or which material lot the failing jobs ran (Q14, Q17 open). Material batch 3 opened at tick 1310 (E6) before job 14's failure, yet jobs 15-18 passed afterward, so batch 3 alone does not explain the failures (H5 unproven); the loading-door opening at 1729-1740 (E8) postdates job 19's failure, so it cannot explain all failures. Root cause is not isolated: CNC-07, material lot, or another condition remain possible.

anomaly: alarm on CNC-03: vibration 5.12 mm/s above 4.50
conclusion: CNC-03 has a genuine mechanical fault, most consistent with a bearing/spindle defect. Vibration jumped from ~0.003 mm/s at tick 70 to about 5.0–5.2 mm/s sustained across ticks 71–78, well above the 4.50 mm/s alarm threshold, then fell back to normal once the machine was stopped (E15). Before tick 70 vibration was normal (E5), nearby CNC-04 is normal (E14) ruling out an external source, and the readings are too sustained and consistent to be a sensor glitch (H2) or spurious alarm (H4). Following error also rose to ~1.8 µm during the event (E12) and power was elevated (E10), supporting an actual axis/mechanical problem rather than a reporting fault. CNC-03 is now idle and has no hydraulics (E3).
